name: Bo Allan
summary: Powerful, ready-made midfielder and half-back who was already playing WAFL League footy as a junior. Breaks tackles and explodes out of stoppages, and was rated elite for speed, agility and strength. His decision making and midfield craft were the parts still developing.

name: Harry Armstrong
summary: Prolific left-footed key forward who kicked an equal-high nine goals at the national championships. Strong on the lead and in the air, with very reliable set shots. Needed to build his tank and stay in games for all four quarters.

name: Leo Lombard
summary: Hard-edged, competitive inside midfielder who also hits the scoreboard, averaging 4.8 clearances and 4.5 tackles at the national championships. High work rate and a big tank. Decision making and temperament were the knocks.

name: Levi Ashcroft
summary: A ball magnet who averaged around 28 disposals across two Talent League seasons and about 30 at the 2024 national championships. Dangerous in attack and rated elite for consistency and ceiling. Shook off tags as the year went on. Top-end speed and temperament were the only real knocks.

name: Joe Berry
summary: Skilful, clinical small-to-medium forward who rose fast in 2024 on the back of four-goal hauls in the Talent League. Finishes from anywhere off both feet and is strong overhead for his size. Still learning the midfield and needed to hold his impact for four quarters.

name: Jesse Dattoli
summary: Versatile, creative midfielder-forward who can hit the scoreboard and played a running wing role for Vic Metro. Covers the ground well and links up in transition. Decision making and set-shot kicking needed work.

name: Alex Dodson
summary: Athletic, late-developing ruck from a basketball background who averaged 19.7 hitouts and 3.7 clearances at the national championships. Clean below his knees and follows up at ground level, with an elite ceiling. Raw, with limited footy exposure and forward craft to build.

name: Sid Draper
summary: Explosive midfielder with the best agility test in the country in 2023. Gets the ball out of congestion at speed with very clean hands, and already showed it at SANFL senior level. Durability and his end product by foot were the question marks.

name: Jonty Faull
summary: Hard-working, mobile key forward who competes in the air and follows up at ground level. Leads well and kicks straight. Composure and contested marking needed to improve.

name: Tom Gross
summary: Physical, explosive midfielder compared with Toby Greene for his mix of power at stoppages and danger forward of centre. Competitive both ways. Disposal was rated below average, and composure and end product were the work-ons.

name: Taj Hotton
summary: Elite athlete with top-three combine-level sprint, leap and agility numbers. Turned from a low-possession forward into a big-ball-winning on-baller in 2024, averaging 116 Talent League fantasy points. Kicking and finishing were the main work-ons.

name: Cooper Hynes
summary: Big-bodied, powerful midfielder-forward who wins contested ball and is clean and creative by hand and foot. Uses his size to break tackles. Speed and endurance were rated below average, so building his running capacity was the key.

name: Isaac Kako
summary: Exciting, creative small forward who can also play high half-forward and win clearances. Elite agility and great at reading ground balls out of a pack. Defensive output and composure were the work-ons.

name: Sam Lalor
summary: A man among boys at 188cm: a powerful, one-touch contested midfielder who also marks strongly and hurts teams forward of centre. Elite strength and an elite ceiling, with hard tackling. Durability and endurance were the concerns, which fits his injury-hit start.

name: Harvey Langford
summary: Tall, strong, all-round midfielder who averaged 6.3 clearances and 6.3 inside 50s at the national championships. Wins his own ball, spreads, kicks long off the left and marks strongly forward. Remarkably consistent. Speed was rated below average.

name: Xavier Lindsay
summary: Elite-kicking midfielder with a raking left foot, as good on the outside as at stoppages. Started as a wing and defender before moving into the midfield. Few weaknesses; durability and inside craft were the only flags.

name: Sam Marshall
summary: Reliable ball-winner with an elite tank, averaging 27 disposals for the Allies and never dropping below 24. Works between contests and carries the ball forward. Opposite foot and a handball-heavy game were the work-ons.

name: Christian Moraes
summary: Consistent, high-volume runner who had 25+ disposals in seven of his 12 Talent League games and kicked multiple goals four times. Elite endurance and dangerous running in waves. Kicking technique (rated below average) and defensive running were the knocks.

name: Harrison Oliver
summary: Possibly the best left-foot kick in the draft: an intercepting half-back who hit 83% efficiency at the national championships and reads the play well. Brave in the air for his size. Needed to win more of the ball and do it for four quarters.

name: Finn O'Sullivan
summary: One of the most complete prospects in the pool: powerful speed and a big leap, booming kicks and the ability to play inside or out, with an elite ceiling. His junior ball-winning numbers were modest (11.5 disposals at the championships) and durability was flagged.

name: Murphy Reid
summary: Poised, classy midfielder with elite disposal and decision making who plays at his own tempo. Consistent week to week and a strong runner. Lacks explosive speed and size.

name: Jobe Shanahan
summary: Versatile, mobile tall who can play key forward, down back or through the midfield, with elite aerial ability and an elite ceiling. Strong overhead and clean hands. Ground balls and follow-up work were the gaps.

name: Thomas Sims
summary: Athletic ruck-forward with strong hands who switched between the ruck and the forward line, and occasionally rucked alone. Marking was the standout. Set shots and scoreboard consistency needed work.

name: Josh Smillie
summary: The most athletic and skilled tall midfielder in the crop at 195cm, with strong stoppage craft. Averaged 5.8 clearances at the national championships. Burst speed and contested marking were the gaps.

name: Jagga Smith
summary: Huge accumulator who averaged 33.8 disposals in the Talent League (a high of 50) and 29 at the national championships, plus a game-high 31 on VFL debut. Runs like Sam Walsh and wins clearances, with elite consistency and ceiling. Lightly framed, and impact per possession was the knock.

name: Alix Tauru
summary: Athletic, versatile tall defender with elite aerial ability who can also play forward. Lots of potential but interrupted by injuries in both junior seasons, so durability was the big question.

name: Luke Trainor
summary: Former forward turned intercepting key defender with an elite leap and strong contested marking; kicked Vic Metro's title-winning goal after being swung forward. Reads the play well. Lockdown defence was still developing.

name: Tobie Travaglia
summary: Elite-running half-back who moved into the midfield late in the year; finished second in the national 2km time trial. Line-breaking speed, intercept marking and lots of follow-up efforts. Disposal was rated below average, and he needed to add size.

name: Jack Whitlock
summary: Mobile, big-marking tall with elite aerial range who leads up the ground and is clean at ground level for a 200cm player. Has a big-game streak. Goalkicking and ruck craft needed work.

name: Matt Whitlock
summary: Very agile, high-ceiling tall who played both ends, kicking 27 goals for Murray while projecting as an intercepting defender. Raw, light-framed and not a one-on-one defender yet.

name: Jasper Alger
summary: One of the best goalsneaks in the crop, kicking goals in every APS game including an eight. A big-game player who finds the goals rather than lots of the ball. Ball-winning and tackling pressure were the work-ons.

name: Cody Anderson
summary: Strong, contested inside midfielder known for bone-crunching tackles and two-way running; averaged 5.7 tackles in the Talent League. Elite contested game and strength. Disposal was rated below average and his outside game was limited.

name: Cody Angove
summary: Clever, skilful link player off half-forward and the wing who sets up scoring chains and is dangerous at ground level. Good speed and endurance. Lightly built, with contested work to improve.

name: James Barrat
summary: Tough, competitive tall who intercepts and plays a physical brand of footy at either end. Came back from a serious injury that wiped out his 2023. Decision making and set shots were the work-ons.

name: Cooper Bell
summary: A 199cm athlete with real speed (2.925-second 20m sprint) who can play key defence, forward or pinch-hit in the ruck. A big-upside, raw project with low junior production and endurance to build.

name: Ned Bowman
summary: Highlight-reel forward with spectacular pack marks, real speed and natural goal sense, who could also develop into an intercepting half-back. A low-possession player who needed to impact for four quarters.

name: Ben Camporeale
summary: Reliable, high-volume ball-winner who averaged 31.7 disposals and won the SANFL U18 best and fairest, and was South Australia's top ball-winner at the national championships. Runs hard to chain possessions. Kicking and defensive effort were the knocks.

name: Lucas Camporeale
summary: Outside ball-winner who runs the wing intelligently and is a constant outlet; Ben's twin and son of Scott. Averaged 25 disposals at SANFL U18 level. Lacks line-breaking speed and contested work.

name: Angus Clarke
summary: Pure footballer who kicks and marks well at both ends, settling as a dashing rebounder who took South Australia's kick-ins. Improving fast, but still raw and short on top-level exposure.

name: Joel Cochran
summary: Mobile, athletic tall defender who won the 2km time trial at the combine and had a top-10 vertical leap. Strong intercept mark and rebounder who can also play forward or ruck. Composure and kicking on the run needed work.

name: Hamish Davis
summary: Versatile midfielder-forward who averaged 22 disposals and kicked 14 goals in nine WAFL Colts games. Clean below his knees, with an elite tank and good bodywork. Explosive speed and kicking action were flagged.

name: Josh Dolan
summary: Energetic small link player at high half-forward with an elite tank and sharp short kicking inside 50. Kicked a goal in all five of his Talent League games. Small, and needed more defensive acts.

name: Kayle Gerreyn
summary: Mobile ruck who projects as a key forward, with a booming two-sided kick, strong contested marking and elite agility for his size. Kicks goals from distance. Endurance (below average) and decision making were the work-ons.

name: Will Hayes
summary: Classic two-way wingman with elite speed, agility and endurance, who also spent time forward. Runs great patterns and uses the ball well. Lightly built, and decision making and goalkicking were the work-ons.

name: Lachie Jaques
summary: Rebounding defender who takes the kick-ins and launches attacks with his kicking; went at 78% efficiency at the national championships. Reads the play and intercepts. Strength and composure were flagged.

name: Noah Mraz
summary: Mobile, skilled key defender who can also ruck and play forward. Clean by hand and foot and reads the play well. Missed much of the year, so he was lightly seen. Needed to add size and speed.

name: Charlie Nicholls
summary: Fast, mobile key forward with elite speed for a 197cm player who leads up as a centre half-forward and can also play back or pinch-hit in the ruck. Good field kick. Set shots and physicality needed work.

name: Harry O'Farrell
summary: Athletic key defender with good positioning, closing speed and intercept marking who can also play forward. Light-framed (strength rated below average), with clean hands and set shots to improve.

name: Jack Ough
summary: Tall, clean midfielder who plays inside or out and uses the ball efficiently, finishing the Talent League season strongly (25+ disposals five times). Uses his size at stoppages. Lacks speed and hurt factor.

name: Logan Smith
summary: Big, strong 204cm ruck with the biggest reach tested at the combine. Won the most hitouts at the national championships and held his own in the VFL. Endurance and speed were both below average.

name: Rhys Unwin
summary: Small forward with an electric turn of speed and outstanding combine pace results, starting to move into the midfield. Strong defensive pressure. Kicking and finishing were the gaps.

name: Luke Urquhart
summary: Big-bodied, powerful inside midfielder with a sub-three-second 20m sprint who wins clearances (5.3 a game) and drives the ball long. Disposal was rated below average, and decision making and durability were flagged.

name: Charlie West
summary: Strong, aggressive forward and undersized ruck whose contested marking is his weapon; had a top-10 vertical jump at the combine. Elite strength. Endurance and field kicking were below average.

name: Riak Andrew
summary: Over-age key defender, Mac Andrew's brother and a Melbourne NGA product, who found a home down back in 2024 with some strong lockdown jobs. Athletic with good speed and aerial ability, but light-framed and still raw.

name: Riley Bice
summary: Mature-age VFL recruit who averaged 21.8 disposals in Werribee's premiership side as a dashing half-back and wingman. Terrific ball use by foot and loves an overlap run. Contested work and strength were the gaps.

name: Hugh Boxshall
summary: Late-rising, big-bodied clearance midfielder with an excellent tank who finished on the podium in the 2km, agility and vertical jump at WA's state combine. Capped his year with 30 disposals in Claremont's Colts premiership. Lacked hurt factor and versatility.

name: Sam Davidson
summary: Mature-age forward and medical student picked out of Gippsland local footy who kicked 26 goals in 17 games in his first VFL season. Blends running power with aerial range and can also play on a wing. Still raw and needed to add size.

name: Lucca Grego
summary: Hard-working, defence-first midfielder and half-back with a rugby league background who applies real pressure and intercepts well. Tidied up his kicking off half-back as the year went on. Composure and goalkicking were the work-ons.

name: Oliver Hannaford
summary: Late bolter after big finals, including a six-goal quarter final. Explosive, all-action utility who topped the state combine agility test and hunts the ball and the opponent hard. Endurance and polish on the run were the work-ons.

name: Lennox Hofmann
summary: St Kilda Next Generation Academy defender who played the roaming intercept role in Sandringham's flag. Very quick for his size (best 20m sprint at the state combine) and reads the play well. One-on-one defending and kicking consistency needed work.

name: Zak Johnson
summary: Northern Knights co-captain and best and fairest winner, and one of the best ball users in the pool, with the speed to break lines. A shoulder injury cut his season short and kept him out of combine testing. Best suited to an outside, second-possession role; contested work and defence were the work-ons.

name: Luke Kennedy
summary: Won a senior best and fairest at 16 and became an underrated engine-room midfielder in Sandringham's premiership. Clean, dual-footed, smart and accountable, with a big tank. Lacks explosive speed and an outside game.

name: Keighton Matofai-Forbes
summary: Western Jets captain and strong-bodied power forward who can also play at half-back. Physical, competitive and a long kick, but his decisions with the ball were inconsistent. Needed to steady in front of goal and rebuild his endurance after injury setbacks.

name: Jacob Molier
summary: Draft smokey after a standout SA combine, with a top-five national 20m sprint for a 201cm ruck. Good ruck craft and real upside. Needed to build his endurance to get involved around the ground and improve his set shots when resting forward.

name: Jay Polkinghorne
summary: Lesser-known SA forward who missed the national carnival after a preseason knee injury but kicked a goal in every game he played, including two in Norwood's reserves premiership. Strong overhead with a reliable set shot. In-between size, and his fitness base needed building.

name: Patrick Said
summary: Classy, well-rounded midfielder-forward who kicked 23 goals in 14 games for Calder, with poise, agility and clean skills. Very consistent junior fantasy scorer. Size was the likely limit as an on-baller, and he could win more of the ball.

name: Tyler Welsh
summary: Adelaide father-son prospect and SA's leading goalkicker at the national carnival. Powerful, aggressive marking forward with good hands and deceptive speed who only needs a few moments to hurt you. Low-volume ball winner; endurance and impact away from the forward 50 were the work-ons.

name: Ty Gallop
summary: Brisbane Academy key forward with a strong mark and goal sense, nearly three goals a game in limited 2024 Talent League games.

name: Jaren Carr
summary: Mature-age utility from South Fremantle’s WAFL side.

name: River Stevens
summary: Tough, pressuring small forward from Geelong Falcons with goal sense; size and kicking consistency the work-ons.

name: Aidan Johnson
summary: Mature-age 193cm ruck-forward from Werribee who played 20 VFL games in 2024.
